name: arm_fadvise
synopsis: long arm_fadvise64_64(int fd, int advice, loff_t offset, loff_t len);
description: The arm_fadvise system call is an architecture-specific variant of posix_fadvise for ARM systems, allowing programs to predeclare an access pattern for file data to optimize kernel performance. It announces expected access patterns for a specified file region, though the advice is not binding.

parameters.name: fd
parameters.description: File descriptor of the file to which the advice applies.

parameters.name: advice
parameters.description: Advice type, such as POSIX_FADV_NORMAL, POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL, etc., indicating the access pattern.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Starting offset of the region in the file.

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the region in bytes, or 0 to indicate until the end of the file.

return_value.failure: Returns an error number on error

errors.description: The fd argument was not a valid file descriptor.
An invalid value was specified for advice.
The specified file descriptor refers to a pipe or FIFO.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.6, if len was specified as 0, it was interpreted as zero bytes rather than through to the end of the file.
versions: Linux 2.6.14 for ARM; kernel support first appeared in Linux 2.5.60
